reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an app with claims that viewers can earn ₹500 per day or up to Rs 5,000, and directs them to register using the creator-provided referral code. The promoted flow includes paid game amounts up to ₹10,000 and presents winnings as instantly withdrawable, while showing a fee deducted before confirmation. An educational disclaimer is countercontext, and the advertised earnings and payout are unverified.

citations.quote: Earn ₹ 500 per day by Playing Ludo
please download this app and register through my referral code
by this App also, you can earn up to Rs 5,000 INR
you can play games for 10 to 10,000 Rs
You can complete your payment through various methods

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful caution rather than an unconditional promise. Viewers are told that earning ₹500 is not automatic and that success depends on Ludo skill: “this doesn't mean you will start playing like this and will start winning this money.” The speaker also advises beginners to start with the least expensive game and increase amounts only as their skill improves. He warns against cheating and explains that penalties or an account ban may follow. These qualifications frame the opportunity as a skill-based, risk-bearing promotion with explicit conduct rules, not a guaranteed payout for everyone.

citations.quote: this doesn't mean you will start playing like this and will start winning this money
i suggest that in starting you start with least amount game
don't cheat If you cheat you were given a penalty or your id is also banned

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account treats promotional headline language as if it were a guarantee, but the spoken qualification expressly rejects that reading: the speaker says viewers will not simply begin playing and winning ₹500. The advice to start with a small amount and the warning about penalties further communicate risk and conditions. A disclaimer is not required to eliminate every positive claim; the relevant question is whether the overall presentation promises effortless results, which these warnings contradict.

citations.quote: this doesn't mean you will start playing like this and will start winning this money
first of all start with less amount

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not neutralize the central solicitation. The title still advertises earning ₹500 per day, while the description directs viewers to download and register through the creator's referral code. Saying skill is needed or advising a smaller starting amount leaves intact the invitation to deposit money and pursue earnings; it does not verify that the advertised income or withdrawal will occur for viewers.

citations.quote: Earn ₹ 500 per day by Playing Ludo
please download this app and register through my referral code
you can play games for 10 to 10,000 Rs

opening.argument: The video's observable format is an operational walkthrough. The speaker says he will explain the process “step by step,” then demonstrates registration, wallet funding, challenge selection, room-code entry, gameplay, and withdrawal. The sampled frames likewise show the presenter alongside the mobile interface, including the wallet, challenges, and withdrawal screens. That is consistent with a tutorial or personal demonstration of how the service operates, not proof that every viewer will obtain the promoted result. The content can therefore be understood as explaining a game-and-wallet workflow whose claims remain for viewers to evaluate.

citations.quote: I'll be telling you step by step, all the process
download that application on your phone and after that install it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the walkthrough contains a referral link does not change its demonstrated subject: the speaker explains how to navigate two applications and connect a Ludo room code. The reference description relies on earnings language, but instructional demonstrations can show claimed functionality without certifying universal results. The footage shows a process and an interface; it does not establish that the creator concealed a failed test or fabricated the screens.

citations.quote: will explain all step by step process to you
you have to go to lodoking wait for some time and if opponent join by entering the same room code here opponent will show up

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not make it neutral. The tutorial repeatedly instructs viewers how to register through the supplied referral, fund a paid challenge, and seek a withdrawal, while presenting the creator's own purported success as evidence. The interface frames show the workflow, but they cannot establish that the service reliably pays viewers or that the claimed earnings are genuine. Operational detail can make a solicitation more actionable rather than educational.

citations.quote: please download this app and register through my referral code
My payment is 50 rupees
As you can see I have added 90 rupees in my my area wallet

opening.argument: The material describes participation in a paid Ludo service and its ordinary account operations: users select a game amount, find an opponent, play, and submit a winning screenshot for review. It does not describe an investment, a downline, or a request for sensitive credentials. The speaker even identifies a transaction charge and shows that the displayed final payment is lower than the winning balance, which is more consistent with a disclosed service fee than a hidden deduction. The evidence supports treating this as a game and payment service promotion, without independently certifying every result.

citations.quote: you can play games for 10 to 10,000 Rs
after uploading the Winning Money and if i win the game
the transaction fee is taken, it is 2.7 rupees transaction charge
Then there will be an OTP on the number

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account labels the flow deceptive without identifying a concealed mechanism. The amount, game process, screenshot verification, and transaction fee are described openly, and the OTP is presented as confirmation of the withdrawal rather than a request for unrelated credentials. The presence of a referral and a paid game may make this a commercial promotion, but those features alone do not establish that the service is fraudulent or that payment is impossible.

citations.quote: in options select option and type and click on submit and after it verifies on admin
the transaction fee is taken, it is 2.7 rupees transaction charge

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The ordinary-service framing omits the material risk: viewers are directed to deposit money into paid challenges while being encouraged by claims of easy earnings and instant withdrawal. A disclosed fee does not validate the underlying service, and an OTP confirms an attempted transaction rather than successful, reliable payout. The absence of a downline or investment pitch is beside the point because the depicted mechanism is direct participation for promised winnings.
